Fillets and chamfers (I3 S3): status

DFMA Review · Inventor I3, slice S3 · 2026-11-09 · branch inventor-i2-s2, draft PR #27 (not merged)

S3 is built and its checks pass. With an .ipt, the app now lists each fillet and chamfer with its size as designed, finds its faces in the STEP, and makes a finding when a fillet's radius differs from the STEP's. The panel and PDF section are as the mock-up you approved (D-043).

Nothing to decide now. There is no new demo for this slice (D-044): the next demo comes from the new step-by-step screen, which is specced and built next. PR #27 still waits for your check of one work pair in Inventor, from 2026-11-12.

What S3 does

  • Reads every fillet and chamfer from the .ipt: fillet radius; chamfer distances and angle. A face copied by a pattern or mirror counts with its fillet.
  • Finds each one's faces in the STEP by shape and place (within 0.01 mm). Tapping a row lights them up.
  • A fillet whose radius differs from the STEP face at its place is a medium finding, "fillet vs face". Chamfers are checked by place only: a STEP file stores the face, not the distances.
  • A blend it can't read (only spline faces, or a near-flat cone) says so: our limit, never a finding.

Measured on the NIST files

  • Fillet and chamfer counts equal the Fillet and Chamfer names stored in every NIST part that has them (CTC 04: 7 fillets and 1 chamfer; CTC 02: 12).
  • On the 11 NIST pairs, 499 of 744 fillet faces are found in the STEP, as the spec measured. No pair gives a fillet finding.
  • Three spec points were corrected while building, each measured: copies are not corner patches; the FTC 11 face the spec called "another radius" sits 0.043 mm elsewhere with the same radius; a face must be near its STEP face, not just on the same plane. All in the spec's S3 "Settled at build".
